newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares stage technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares stage technical rebound.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share markets saw a technical rebound during the Thursday morning session, spurred by bargain-hunting after Wednesday's steep drops, brokers said.
The foreign currency B share index was up 1.11 points or 0.78 percent at 143.47 on turnover of HK$16.3 million.
The domestic currency A share index rallied 0.36 points or 0.09 percent to 415.10. Turnover was a thin 2.4 billion yuan.
Both indices ended sharply lower on Wednesday on panic selling fuelled by apprehension over possible further Beijing crackdown measures on speculative trading, brokers said.
"The morning's markets were supported by sporadic bargain-hunting, but investors remained wary judging by the thin turnover," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
Brokers said they foresaw volatile trading ahead amid concerns over further clampdowns.
"I would advise investors to wait for a few more sessions before starting to buy or sell," a J&A Securities analyst said.

Strings of anti-speculation measures, ranging from a huge 30 billion yuan new share quota for 1997 to the latest ban on banks from entering the equity markets, have dealt heavy blows to the stock markets, traders said.
On the B share market, colour television maker Konka Group was the heaviest gainer with a rise of HK$0.51 or 4.77 percent to HK$11.20.
Beihai Xinli, which handles port facilities in the southwestern province of Guangxi, surged 0.78 yuan or 6.61 percent to 12.58 yuan to become the session's strongest performing A share.
